full_judgment:
Mr. M. M. Ruhul Amin, J: This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and decree dated 25.02.2000 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in 2nd Appeal No. 327 of 1978 allowing the appeal, setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court as well as the Court of appeal decreeing the plaintiffs suit for declaration of title to the suit land described in schedule 'Ka', 'Kha' & 'G' to the plaint, confirmation of possession in the  land of schedule 'Ka' and recovery of Khas possession of the land in schedules 'Kha' and `Ga'. 

 4. The defendant No. I contested the suit by filing a written statement he denied the material allegations made in the plaint. His case, in short is that the superior landlord Biseswar Saha and others never auction purchased the suit land and they also never took delivery of Khas possession through Court. His further case is that he has been possessing the suit land from the time of his grandfather and they were never evicted from the suit land by the landlords. 

 11. Both the trial. Court and appellate Court concurrently held that Biseswar Saha and others auction purchased the suit land and took delivery of possession through court. Although no sale certificate or the writ for delivery of possession could be produced, the plaintiffs filed Ext.4(c) the certified copy o judgment and decree passed in Title suit No. 88 of 1924 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Khulna filed by landlords, Biseswar Saha and another against the father of present defendant No. 1 and others and got a decree for recovery of Khas possession in the suit land after evicting the defendants including the father of the defendant No. 1. Ext. 8, certified copy of a petition filed by the present defendant No. 1 against Jaz Ali, father of the present plaintiff and others in Criminal case No. 2227 of 1967 and in this petition the defendant No. 1 admitted the auction purchase by Biseswar Saha, defendant No.6 and others. Ext. 6 (a) is deposition of defendant No 1. in the above criminal case and this shows that the defendant No. 1 admitted that the landlords Biseswar Saha auction purchased the suit land. Defendant No. 1 further in his evidence stated that he possessed the suit land by taking amicable settlement from the landlord, defendant No.6.
